title: Computation of the sequential derived inverse limit
statement:
Let $\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T)$ be the tower category of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and let $M_\bullet\in
D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$. If $M_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ is a K-injective
resolution [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] of $M_\bullet$ in the
abelian category of towers, then $\varprojlim_nI_n$ represents the sequential
derived inverse limit $\Rlim M_\bullet$ of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit]..

proof.text: Unpack the tower category and the sequential derived inverse limit using [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit]. The K-injective terminology is the generic sheaf-of-modules notion of [def-pur-kinjective-complex], specialized to the site $T_{\Proet}$ and the ring sheaf $A_T$; [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] records the same resolution convention in the constant étale setting. The ring-sheaf module category $\Mod(A_T)$ is Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], hence has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Together with the exact countable products supplied in [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit], these are the hypotheses of clause (3) of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence]. Applying that clause to the evaluation system $(\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet)$ and its K-injective representative $I_\bullet$ gives the termwise inverse-limit complex $\varprojlim_n I_n$ as a derived limit. The derived-limit notation and its Roos triangle are those of [def-weil-derived-limit], so uniqueness up to isomorphism identifies this object with $\Rlim M_\bullet$.

lean.statement:
theorem derivedCategory_towerLimit_core
    (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [HasCountableProducts A] [CountableAB4Star A]
    (hP : HasCountableProducts (DerivedCategory A)) :
    letI : HasCountableProducts (DerivedCategory A) := hP
    ∀ (_ : EnoughInjectives A)
      (I : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective]
      (K : ℕ → DerivedCategory A) (f : ∀ n : ℕ, K (n + 1) ⟶ K n)
      (_e : I.asFunctor ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅ Functor.ofOpSequence f),
      ∃ c : Cone I.asFunctor, Nonempty (IsLimit c) ∧
        IsDerivedLimit f (DerivedCategory.Q.obj c.pt)
lean.note: The existing general K-injective tower computation, specialized to B = Mod(A_T), K n = ev_(n+1) M, and the inherited transitions. A K-injective tower resolution supplies I.IsKInjective and the natural representation isomorphism e, including transition compatibility. EnoughInjectives B follows from the cited Grothendieck theorem; exact countable products and derived products follow from the existing dependencies. The actual limit cone c supplies the termwise inverse-limit complex and IsDerivedLimit is exactly the sequential Roos property. This reuses the published theorem already reached by clause (3) of lem-weil-derived-limit-existence; no alternate coefficient category or new construction is introduced.

D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$. If $M_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ is a K-injective
resolution [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] of $M_\bullet$ in the
abelian category of towers, then $\varprojlim_nI_n$ represents the sequential
derived inverse limit $\Rlim M_\bullet$ of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit].

proof.text:
By [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] the object $\Rlim M_\bullet$ is the
derived limit of the inverse system $(\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet)$ in the
triangulated category $D(T_{\Proet},A)$ attached to the tower category of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], an abelian category with exact
countable products. Clause (3) of the derived-limit existence lemma of the
conventions chapter states that a K-injective representative of the system in
the abelian category of towers represents its derived limit; applying it to
the system $(\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet)$ and its K-injective
representative $I_\bullet$ exhibits $\varprojlim_nI_n$ as a derived limit of
the system, and clause (1) of the same lemma shows that any two derived
limits of one system are isomorphic.
